currency.mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. Prior path: 13.25% held at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug); 25bps cut from 13.50% at the May 2026 MPC; 75bps cut from 14.25% on 11 Feb 2026. The 30 Sep decision coincided with the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect and the start of IMF successor-programme talks.

trendAnalysis.direction: USD/ZMW market mid 20.2741 — 0.61% softer than the 12 Oct snapshot (20.1503) and +1.20% above the 26 Oct level. BoZ official mid 20.201 on 30 Oct (vs 20.1450 on 26 Oct), so the market is trading ~0.4% above the official fix. The kwacha has spent late October consolidating in a 20.10–20.30 band after the September break above 19.80.
drivers: Record copper output ~890K tonnes (2025) — strong export earnings
Record maize harvest >4M tonnes — reduced food import needs
Debt restructuring ~94% complete — sovereign risk premium compressing
IMF successor programme talks under way (ECF) after the final review completed; new US$1.47bn staff-level agreement reached
BoZ cut the MPR 250bps to 10.75% on 30 September 2026 as inflation eased back into the target band — the lowest policy rate in several years
10% copper-concentrate export duty took effect 30 September 2026
Yuan mining tax corridor reducing USD demand
Gross international reserves near record highs (~US$5.5bn)
Policy continuity after the 1 Sep 2026 inauguration of President Hichilema and Vice-President for a second term
BoZ cut statutory reserve requirements (early Aug 2026) — supportive of bank liquidity
KCM copper output up 21% in H1 2026 — supportive of the mining/export outlook
trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha is consolidating rather than trending. The USD/ZMW market mid sits at ~K20.27 (open.er-api.com, 30 Oct) versus ~K20.15 in the 12 Oct snapshot, a modest +0.61% softening, while the BoZ official fix has edged from 20.1450 (26 Oct) to 20.201 (30 Oct). The move is mixed across the basket: sterling costs 1.38% more kwacha and the yuan 1.59% more, but the euro and rand are flat and the pula is actually 2.06% cheaper, which points to cross-currency noise rather than one-way kwacha selling. Support still comes from record copper output and export earnings, reserves near US$5.5bn, a near-complete debt restructuring and the US$1.47bn IMF staff-level agreement. The offset is a materially easier policy stance after the 30 September 2026 MPC cut the MPR 250bps to 10.75% with inflation back inside the 6-8% band, plus the 10% copper-concentrate export duty that took effect the same day. Watch copper prices, end-of-month corporate USD demand and the pace of further BoZ easing over the coming sessions.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 19.20–20.50 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.50–20.50 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
